title.narrative: Supporting Private Sector and Financial Market Reforms

description.narrative: The grant will assist the Government implement the Program. Specifically, it will help the Government (i) strengthen the legal framework, (ii) remove market distortions, (iii) disengage the Government from commercial activities, (iv) strengthen financial intermediation, and (v) implement accounting and auditing standards. The grant will also develop and establish training programs in these areas to help sustain private sector and financial market development over the long term.
Dynamic private sector and Improved financial intermediation

1. Dynamic private sector Increased private sector share in industrial production (from 26% in 2005 to approximately 40% in 2009) Increased private investment rate (from 8.5% in 2005 to approximately 14% in 2011) Increased private saving rate (from 2.3% in 2005 to approximately 8% in 2011) Increased number of registered private enterprises Data Source: Economic and statistical reports by CSO, DAB and IMF, and World Bank Statistics of business registration and licensing in Afghanistan Investment Support Agency (AISA), Ministry of Commerce (MOC) and major municipal governments Asian Development Bank (ADB) review missions

2. Improved financial intermediation
Increased access to bank credit (from 1.2% of GDP in 2005 to approximately 5% in 2009 ) Higher deposit mobilization (from 3.6% of GDP in 2005 to approximately 11% in 2009) Longer maturity of bank loans and deposits (from a maximum of 6 months in 2005 to at least 1 year in 2009) Lower borrowing costs Data Source: Economic and statistical reports by CSO, DAB and IMF, and World Bank Statistics of business registration and licensing in Afghanistan Investment Support Agency (AISA), Ministry of Commerce (MOC) and major municipal governments Asian Development Bank (ADB) review missions
